8	# Local Hebrew PII detection
9	
10	Ask a locally-running model whether a piece of Hebrew text contains personal data. No network call, no data leaves the machine.
11	
12	The hard part is not finding an ID number. It is that many Hebrew given names are ordinary words. `אורן` is a pine tree, `אריאל` is a city, `גיל` is age, `עמית` is a colleague, `עידן` is an era, `שחר` is dawn. Names also wear one-letter prefixes, so `לאייל` is "to Eyal" and `משחר` is "from Shahar". A detector must read how a word is used, not whether it could be a name.
13	
14	## Use it
15	
16	Every entry point takes either raw text or a path to a file holding the text.
17	
18	```bash
19	./pii_detect.py "דיברתי היום עם ריקי אלמוזנינו. הנייד שלה 054-7712398."   # -> YES
20	./pii_detect.py notes/meeting.txt                                        # reads the file
21	echo "האורן שליד הגדר נראה יבש, כדאי לבדוק השקיה." | ./pii_detect.py       # -> NO
22	echo "notes/meeting.txt" | ./pii_detect.py                               # reads the file
23	```

26	from pii_detect import detect_pii
27

1	# Synthetic messages, turns, and delivery lifecycle
2	
3	Use this model whenever an extension injects information into a Pi session. The crucial distinction is not visual presentation; it is whether the payload becomes an agent message at all.
4	
5	## Choose the channel by who must know
6	
7	### `pi.appendEntry()` is for the user alone
8	
9	`pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` persists extension data in the session but **never adds it to LLM context**. Pair it with `pi.registerEntryRenderer()` to show durable TUI content in the transcript.
10	
11	Use this when the main agent must remain permanently oblivious. This is the only transcript-visible channel with that guarantee.
12	
13	- Entries survive reloads.
14	- Entry renderer `data` is optional in the SDK type; guard it.
15	- Rendering an entry does not make it a message.
16	- `display: false` on a custom message is not an alternative: hiding UI does not hide content from the LLM.
17	
18	### `pi.sendMessage()` always creates agent-visible context
19	
20	`pi.sendMessage()` creates a custom synthetic message. Its `content` participates in LLM context. `deliverAs` and `triggerTurn` control *when* the agent receives it, not *whether* the agent receives it.
21	
22	Never use `sendMessage()` for information the main agent must not eventually see. In particular, `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` means “later,” not “never.”
23	
24	### `pi.sendUserMessage()` impersonates a user turn
25	
26	`pi.sendUserMessage()` creates an actual user-role message and always triggers agent work. When idle it starts a turn immediately. When streaming, the caller must choose `deliverAs: "steer"` or `"followUp"`.
27	
28	Prefer a custom message when synthetic provenance matters. Use `sendUserMessage()` only when the extension intentionally wants the same semantics as user-authored input.

13

15	
16	```
17	 browser ── React + assistant-ui (Next, web/) ──HTTP+SSE──▶ bridge (Node, bridge/) ──in-proc──▶ Pi SDK

25	  pushes a **snapshot** to subscribed SSE clients. Pi stays the source of truth; the React side
26	  is a near-trivial store that just renders snapshots. History and resume come for free (the
27	  first SSE frame on (re)connect is the full snapshot). `projection.mjs` is the Pi→assistant-ui
28	  translation (the one module that tracks Pi's event/message shapes).
